`CachedPartFolderAccess::CacheParams::explain_enabled` defaults to `false`; when disabled, `recordDecision` takes neither the journal mutex nor a journal allocation, while `getView` computes one cache key and reuses it.

`registerContentAddressedMetadataStorage` must use the `gcs_max_conditional_put_bytes_` member name, throw `DB::Exception` with `NO_ELEMENTS_IN_CONFIG` when `server_root_id` is missing, and reconcile the `cas_` prefix on part-folder-cache keys.

topic: Consolidated The measured decision is to retain the factory default `dedup_cac
canonical_claim: The measured decision is to retain the factory default `dedup_cache_bytes` of 67108864 bytes (64 MiB); 256 MiB produced flat `CasBlobHead`, `CasBlobBodyPutAvoided`, PUT-class, and hit-rate results, so `MetadataStorageFactory.cpp:267` remains unchanged. Additionally, The Round-B plan defines `dedup_cache_bytes` as an existing cache setting with a documented 64 MiB default and proposes measuring 64 MiB, 256 MiB, and 1 GiB variants. Additionally, `deduplication_cache_bytes` defaults to 64 MiB, and `deduplication_head_first_min_bytes` defaults to 1 MiB with `0` disabling the pre-upload `HEAD`. Additionally, The CAS settings are named `deduplication_cache_bytes`, `deduplication_head_first_min_bytes`, and `gc_snapshot_generations_to_keep`; no compatibility alias for the former abbreviated names is provided.

topic: Consolidated The proposed `part_folder_validate` setting has modes `always`, `
canonical_claim: The proposed `part_folder_validate` setting has modes `always`, `age <X>`, and `never`; `always` is the current and default behavior, `age <X>` skips a body-validation `HEAD` for views validated within X seconds, and `never` removes the body re-proof while leaving `StrictValidate` callers unchanged. Additionally, The Round-B plan defines `part_folder_validate` as a string setting with `always`, `age <N>`, and `never` modes, defaulting to `always`. Additionally, `part_folder_validate` defaults to `always`, also accepts `never` or `age <seconds>`, and controls how often a `ForceFresh` read re-proves a cached manifest body with `HEAD`.

Rev.6 defines the observation threshold as `mount_lease_ttl_ms + mount_lease_ttl_ms/20 + poll_interval_ms`, sets `materialization_grace_ms` to 30000 by default, uses seal id `RefTxnId{my_epoch - 1, UINT64_MAX}`, and bumps snapshot codec version 1 to 2 with `sealed_from`. Additionally, `materialization_grace_ms` is a `PoolConfig` setting with default 30000 and an XML key of the same name; an unclean or fenced mount boundary waits this grace before trusting recovery listings, while a clean boundary skips the wait. Additionally, `materialization_grace_ms` defaults to 30000 ms and is configurable.

The default `content_addressed_log` configuration should include `partition_by`, `max_size_rows`, `reserved_size_rows`, `buffer_size_rows_flush_threshold`, and `flush_on_crash`, while its `<ttl>` is a commented-out example.

topic: Consolidated The v2 ref-ledger budget uses an item cap of 1000, `ref_txn_max_o
canonical_claim: The v2 ref-ledger budget uses an item cap of 1000, `ref_txn_max_ops` of 5000, and a per-operation encoded-size cap of 4 KiB; normal `ref_txn_max_bytes` is removed. Additionally, Normal ref-ledger admission uses `ref_txn_max_ops` 5000 and `kMaxRefBatch` 1000; the former byte-estimate admission and give-back spill are not used. Additionally, The normal-class whole-transaction decode cap is 20 MiB, the removal-class byte budget is 64 MiB via `ref_removal_max_bytes`, and normal-class operations have a 4 KiB per-operation cap enforced at admission and decode. Additionally, Stage-1 ref admission uses a 4096-byte per-op limit checked both during admission and decode, a 20 MiB normal-class decode cap plus writer runtime throw, and a 64 MiB `ref_removal_max_bytes` budget with no op cap for removal-class transactions.

Additionally, The parallel-write implementation plan uses `cas_commit_concurrency` default 16 and a process-wide dedicated `cas_commit_pool_size` default 100, separate from the writer pool.

topic: Consolidated Stage 1 adds one server-level CAS upload-pool size setting and re
canonical_claim: Stage 1 adds one server-level CAS upload-pool size setting and rejects an uninitialized or zero-sized pool; non-CAS disks and engines have no behavior change. Additionally, The stage-1 pool setting `content_addressed_blob_upload_pool_size` defaults to 16, rejects 0, and the pool getter throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` before server or test initialization.

The condemned-upload memory setting `content_addressed_condemned_upload_memory_bytes` defaults to 0, meaning derived capacity of pool size multiplied by 64 MiB; the semaphore releases its permit only after `putOverwrite` returns and the body is destroyed. Additionally, The 64 MiB CAS upload value is a chosen default per-task memory budget, not a blob-body size cap; blob bodies are uncapped and an overweight body is admitted exclusively using its actual header-plus-source weight.
